config.mpegtsHint: Service identifiers and transport-stream parameters. Required for strict middleware (Otrum) and hospitality TVs (LG Pro:Centric etc.). Defaults are fine for a single channel — if you run multiple channels on the same multicast subnet, assign distinct Service IDs.
config.serviceNameHint: Shown in the channel list on the receiver (SDT service_name).
config.serviceProviderHint: Broadcaster name (SDT service_provider). Examples: "LiveQX", hotel name.
config.serviceIdHint: program_number in PAT. Range 1..65535. Channels sharing a multicast subnet MUST have distinct Service IDs, otherwise middleware collapses them into one program.
config.transportStreamIdHint: TSID of the transport stream (SDT/PAT). Range 1..65535.
config.originalNetworkIdHint: ONID of the source network (SDT). Usually 1 for private networks; a registered value for public ones.
config.muxRateHint: Constant mux rate: 0 = VBR (default), >0 = enables null-packet stuffing to the given rate. Set to video bitrate + audio bitrate + ~15 % headroom for strict middleware.
config.sdtPeriodHint: SDT repeat period. 0 = FFmpeg default (500 ms). Some middleware wants ≤ 2000 ms.
config.patPeriodHint: PAT/PMT repeat period. 0 = FFmpeg default (100 ms). Strict middleware expects 40–100 ms.
config.videoCodecHint: H.264 is the default for modern receivers. MPEG-2 is only for legacy hospitality set-tops that don't decode H.264 reliably. MPEG-2 is always CPU-encoded — any GPU mode is ignored when this is selected.
config.presetNotApplicableMpeg2: MPEG-2 has no x264-style preset; only bitrate applies.
config.audioCodecHint: AAC-LC is the default for modern receivers and OTT. MP2 (MPEG-1 Layer II) is the classic DVB audio codec for hospitality set-tops that lack AAC licensing or read the PMT stream_type strictly.
config.maxBHintH264: 0 disables B-frames (lowest latency). 2–3 is a good default for OTT/live. Higher values improve compression at the cost of decode delay.
config.maxBHintMpeg2: DVB and set-top boxes traditionally expect the IBBP cadence (2 B-frames). Values above 2 are technically valid but may confuse legacy hardware decoders. 0 disables B-frames entirely.
config.gopSizeHintH264: Distance between key-frames. 0 = auto (equal to FPS, ≈ 1 s). Larger values improve compression; smaller values reduce channel-switch delay. HLS/OTT often uses 2×FPS for finer seek granularity.
config.gopSizeHintMpeg2: Distance between key-frames. 0 = auto (max(FPS/2, 6), i.e. ~0.5 s — the DVB set-top expectation). Broadcast IPTV typically uses 12–15 frames at 25 fps.
config.h264ProfileHint: H.264 profile constraint. Middleware/set-top boxes may require a specific profile: cheap hospitality decoders often lock to Main@3.1; modern boxes handle High. Wrong profile = decode failure. Baseline forces CABAC off (poor compression).
config.h264LevelHint: H.264 level caps bitrate, buffer size and frame dimensions the decoder must support. Match to your resolution/FPS: 3.1 for SD, 4.0 for 1080p 30, 4.2 for 1080p 60, 5.1 for 4K 30. Wrong level = non-compliant stream some decoders refuse.
config.mpeg2ProfileHint: MPEG-2 profile constraint. Consumer DVB/IPTV set-tops universally decode Main (MP) — that is the SD broadcast norm. Simple (SP) drops B-frames for cheap decoders. High (HP) adds SNR scalability rarely used in practice. 4:2:2 is a studio contribution profile — do not use for delivery.
config.mpeg2LevelHint: MPEG-2 level caps resolution and bitrate. Counter-intuitively, LOWER ordinal means HIGHER capability (spec quirk): Low=10 (352×288), Main=8 (720×576/480, ≤15 Mbps — SD DVB), High-1440=6 (1440×1152, ≤60 Mbps), High=4 (1920×1152, ≤80 Mbps). MP@ML (main/8) is the safe default for SD DVB-C/S/T set-tops.
config.bitrateModeVbr: variable with peak ceiling (unicast, HLS, RTMP)
config.bitrateModeHint: CBR is mandatory for MPEG-TS multicast — the fixed VBV envelope is what set-top boxes and hospitality decoders rely on. VBR gives better quality-per-byte on unicast delivery (HLS/RTMP) but breaks MPEG-TS PCR timing. CRF is a quality target for OTT/archive; on GPU and MPEG-2 backends it silently downgrades to VBR (backend logs a warning).
config.bitrateMaxHint: Ceiling for VBR mode in kbps. 0 = auto (encoder picks 1.5×bitrate — enough headroom for scene changes without doubling the pipe width). Ignored outside VBR.
config.crfHint: Constant Rate Factor: lower = better quality, larger file. Sensible range 18..28; 23 is libx264 default. 0 = default. Only meaningful on x264 — GPU and MPEG-2 backends fall back to VBR.
config.preloadSecHint: How many seconds to prefetch from the source. Applied on next channel start.
config.timezoneHint: IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Moscow). Used to interpret schedule windows. Applied on next channel start.
config.modeNoneHint: Channel doesn't read files from disk. Plays only the live source — e.g. a transcoded SRT relay.
config.modePassthroughHint: Files are read straight from the given directory. New files appear instantly, but a share outage takes the channel offline.
config.modeCacheHint: Background daemon syncs share → local cache; the channel plays from cache. Resilient to network drops, but consumes disk space.
config.sinkNoneHint: Nothing is recorded. You can't reconstruct what played and when.
config.sinkFileHint: Daily JSONL files under the channel's playback/ directory. Read with grep/tail; rotation is manual.
config.sinkDbHint: Shared SQLite for all channels. Fast search and reports; entries older than N days are auto-purged.
config.stoppedRequired: Channel must be stopped to edit this section.
config.rawHint: Submit a JSON patch (RFC 7396). Server rejects immutable fields (resolution, fps, id, name) and refuses outputs[] mutations — use /outputs endpoints.

tls.title: TLS
tls.httpInsecure: Plain HTTP — control-plane is not encrypted
tls.modeAutoDesc: Internal CA + server cert managed by the engine. Clients must trust the CA below.
tls.modeProvidedDesc: Operator-supplied cert/key. Use Import to update; the engine never overwrites your PKI on its own.
tls.modeBehindProxyDesc: TLS terminates upstream (nginx / Caddy / Traefik). Core listens plain HTTP only inside the trusted perimeter.
tls.modeDisabledDesc: TLS disabled. Allowed on loopback or with allow_insecure_bind=true. Do not use in production.
tls.caHint: Distribute this PEM to users so their browsers trust the engine. Each download is recorded in the audit log (tls.ca_export).
tls.subject: Subject
tls.regenerateHint: Re-issues server.crt under the existing CA. Listener restarts immediately; the CA stays unchanged so existing user trust survives.
tls.regenerateUnavailable: Available only in `auto` mode. Current mode: {{mode}}.
tls.regenerateConfirm: This will re-issue the server certificate and immediately restart the TLS listener. Continue?
tls.importDescription: Upload an operator-supplied cert + private key (and optional CA). The engine validates the keypair and chain before promoting; old files stay untouched on failure.
tls.importHint: PEM files only. The private key gets chmod 0600 after promotion. Listener restarts on success.
tls.serverKeyHint: Matching private key. Stored with mode 0600.
tls.importCaHint: If provided, the engine verifies the chain cert→ca and refuses on mismatch.

gateways.title: Gateways
gateways.createSubtitle: Configure a new ingest gateway. The gateway starts in stopped state.
gateways.name: Name
gateways.deleteWarning: This stops all flows and removes the gateway configuration. Cannot be undone.
gateways.rebindHint: Address/port/interface changes require stop → patch → start (socket rebind).

fec.label: FEC (forward error correction)
fec.editorHint: Toggling enabled or saving any field hot-swaps the gateway (brief stop → re-create → start).
fec.hotSwapWarn: Save will briefly stop the gateway and restart with the new FEC config. Output ports may change if column/row offsets are edited.

modePlain.passthrough: Takes an incoming stream and forwards it to one or several addresses as-is. Doesn't inspect payload, adds minimal latency. Use it when you just need to fan out a signal.
modePlain.demux: The incoming stream carries several TV channels bundled together (typical for satellite or DVB). The gateway splits them into individual channels and sends each to its own address.
modePlain.remux: The opposite of Demux: takes several separate channels and combines them into one bundled stream. This is how cable operators broadcast.
modePlain.transcode: Re-encodes video and audio with new parameters (bitrate, resolution, codec). The most resource-intensive mode — noticeably loads CPU or GPU.

form.demuxPlain: Each route says which channel (by service_id from the incoming multiplex) goes to which of your outputs. Add one route per channel you want to keep.
form.remuxPlain: The output is a single combined multiplex assembled from every input. The IDs below are service identifiers for PSI tables; usually the defaults are fine.
form.transcodePlain: Bitrate is in bits per second (4,000,000 = 4 Mbps). Resolution, FPS, GPU and encoder presets are configured on the gateway page after creation.
form.fecPlain: Recovers lost packets on the receiver side. Useful on unstable links. Adds roughly 10–25% to bandwidth usage.
form.demuxHint: Each route maps an input service_id to an output ID. Add at least one route.
form.demuxEmpty: No routes — add at least one to demultiplex.
form.targetBitrateHint: 0 = no NULL stuffing. Set ≥ Σ(inputs) for CBR.
form.transcodeHint: Codec settings (resolution, fps, GPU, presets) live in the Detail page after creation.
form.fecPassthroughWarn: FEC for passthrough is not supported yet — use Demux mode with a single * route as workaround.
form.addressInputHint: 0.0.0.0 binds all NICs; multicast group requires a valid join address.
form.ifaceHint: Pick a NIC by name to bind explicitly. Leave empty for kernel default.
form.autostartHint: If enabled, the gateway starts automatically on core boot.
